# Krakow vs Warszawa

## Krakow

Krakow's contract is more explicit on long-horizon fleet-conversion targets. It targets a 74% electric-bus share by 2040, equivalent to roughly 452 new electric buses. [ref_1] The charging rollout is also concrete: Krakow plans at least 150 new public charging stations in the first five years of the programme. [ref_2] For bus operations, it also specifies pantograph charging at Luzycka, Stojalowskiego, and Rydygiera streets. [ref_3]

## Warszawa

Warszawa shows stronger near-term implementation progress. It already operates more than 160 electric buses, signed a 2023 contract for 12 additional electric buses, and is testing hydrogen buses. [ref_4] Its contract also frames transport decarbonisation through expansion of public transport with zero-emission buses and replacement of the bus fleet with electric and hydrogen vehicles. [ref_5] On quantified commitments, Warszawa targets 202 electric buses citywide by 2025, identifies further replacement needs in Praga-Poludnie and Ursynow, and budgets PLN 28.8 million for charging infrastructure on 48 loops. [ref_6] The wider bus-electrification package totals PLN 979.84 million with expected reductions of 144,555 tCO2e. [ref_7]

## Comparison

Krakow is stronger on 2040 fleet and charging targets, while Warszawa is stronger on near-term implementation status and budgeted mission-district investment. Krakow's evidence emphasizes long-range electrification scale and charger rollout; Warszawa's evidence emphasizes current deployment, 2025 bus targets, and funded infrastructure.
